PANINI ALBUM — /club/collection

The spine is PAGES: a fixed nine slots per page, ordered alphabetically by display name, 63 players = 7 pages. Desktop shows a two-page spread, mobile one leaf; page numbers are identical on both.

This is what makes the archetype skew harmless. Archetype stops being the structure and becomes a LENS — pick one and the album re-paginates to just those players.

"Specialists 14" is the useful cut: the people who actually chose a type. The other 49 are All-rounders by default, which is why every one of their cards shows six identical numbers.

Slot numbers are positional, not permanent: a new player joining mid-alphabet shifts every number after them.

CHRONICLE INDEX — /chronicle

Replaces /sessions. The latest issue gets the front page; earlier ones are a back-issue run.

Only weeks with a published session appear — note the jump from issue 12 (week of 17 Aug) to issue 11 (week of 3 Aug). That week had no TFH session, so nothing happened to anyone's rating and there is no issue. No placeholder row.

Issue 11 also shows the no-crossings case: greyed, not hidden, because the row still has its attendance to report.

CHRONICLE ISSUE — /chronicle/2026-08-31

One issue per ISO football week; both sessions nested as matchday reports.

v1 blocks only: matchdays + scorers + bibs, then tier crossings (promotions).

The crossings block is omitted entirely — no empty heading — when there is nothing to say.

RATING HISTORY — /players/[slug]

Replaces the RatingHistory sparkline. Hand-drawn SVG: the app's CSP (style-src 'self' nonce) strips inline style, which rules out every charting library.

Fixed tier-band domain, never auto-fit to the data.

The desktop artboard carries a second panel: the one-point state almost everyone sees at launch.
